  1926	    def resolve_ref(self, name, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False):
  1927	        annotation = self.annotations.get(name)
  1928	        if annotation is not None:
  1929	            if not allow_joins:
  1930	                for alias in self._gen_col_aliases([annotation]):
  1931	                    if isinstance(self.alias_map[alias], Join):
  1932	                        raise FieldError(
  1933	                            "Joined field references are not permitted in this query"
  1934	                        )
  1935	            if summarize:
  1936	                # Summarize currently means we are doing an aggregate() query
  1937	                # which is executed as a wrapped subquery if any of the
  1938	                # aggregate() elements reference an existing annotation. In
  1939	                # that case we need to return a Ref to the subquery's annotation.
  1940	                if name not in self.annotation_select:
  1941	                    raise FieldError(
  1942	                        "Cannot aggregate over the '%s' alias. Use annotate() "
  1943	                        "to promote it." % name
  1944	                    )
  1945	                return Ref(name, self.annotation_select[name])
  1946	            else:
  1947	                return annotation
  1948	        else:
  1949	            field_list = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
  1950	            annotation = self.annotations.get(field_list[0])
  1951	            if annotation is not None:
  1952	                for transform in field_list[1:]:
  1953	                    annotation = self.try_transform(annotation, transform)
  1954	                return annotation
  1955	            join_info = self.setup_joins(
  1956	                field_list, self.get_meta(), self.get_initial_alias(), can_reuse=reuse
  1957	            )

  1960	            )
  1961	            if not allow_joins and len(join_list) > 1:

  1976	    def split_exclude(self, filter_expr, can_reuse, names_with_path):
  1977	        """
  1978	        When doing an exclude against any kind of N-to-many relation, we need
  1979	        to use a subquery. This method constructs the nested query, given the
  1980	        original exclude filter (filter_expr) and the portion up to the first
  1981	        N-to-many relation field.
  1982	
  1983	        For example, if the origin filter is ~Q(child__name='foo'), filter_expr
  1984	        is ('child__name', 'foo') and can_reuse is a set of joins usable for
  1985	        filters in the original query.
  1986	
  1987	        We will turn this into equivalent of:
  1988	            WHERE NOT EXISTS(
  1989	                SELECT 1
  1990	                FROM child
  1991	                WHERE name = 'foo' AND child.parent_id = parent.id
  1992	                LIMIT 1
  1993	            )
  1994	        """
  1995	        # Generate the inner query.
  1996	        query = self.__class__(self.model)
  1997	        query._filtered_relations = self._filtered_relations
  1998	        filter_lhs, filter_rhs = filter_expr
  1999	        if isinstance(filter_rhs, OuterRef):
  2000	            filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs)
  2001	        elif isinstance(filter_rhs, F):
  2002	            filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs.name)
  2003	        query.add_filter(filter_lhs, filter_rhs)
  2004	        query.clear_ordering(force=True)
  2005	        # Try to have as simple as possible subquery -> trim leading joins from
  2006	        # the subquery.
  2007	        trimmed_prefix, contains_louter = query.trim_start(names_with_path)
  2008	
  2009	        col = query.select[0]
  2010	        select_field = col.target
  2011	        alias = col.alias
  2012	        if alias in can_reuse:
  2013	            pk = select_field.model._meta.pk
  2014	            # Need to add a restriction so that outer query's filters are in effect for
  2015	            # the subquery, too.
  2016	            query.bump_prefix(self)
  2017	            lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
  2018	            # Note that the query.select[0].alias is different from alias
  2019	            # due to bump_prefix above.
  2020	            lookup = lookup_class(pk.get_col(query.select[0].alias), pk.get_col(alias))
  2021	            query.where.add(lookup, AND)
  2022	            query.external_aliases[alias] = True
  2023	        else:
  2024	            lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
  2025	            lookup = lookup_class(col, ResolvedOuterRef(trimmed_prefix))
  2026	            query.where.add(lookup, AND)
  2027	
  2028	        condition, needed_inner = self.build_filter(Exists(query))
  2029	
  2030	        if contains_louter:
  2031	            or_null_condition, _ = self.build_filter(
  2032	                ("%s__isnull" % trimmed_prefix, True),
  2033	                current_negated=True,
  2034	                branch_negated=True,
  2035	                can_reuse=can_reuse,
  2036	            )
  2037	            condition.add(or_null_condition, OR)
  2038	            # Note that the end result will be:
  2039	            #   NOT EXISTS (inner_q) OR outercol IS NULL
  2040	            # this might look crazy but due to how NULL works, this seems to be
  2041	            # correct. If the IS NULL check is removed, then if outercol
  2042	            # IS NULL we will not match the row.
  2043	        return condition, needed_inner
